text: dsh-turn-doctor 是一个面向 DSH TUI 的回合故障诊断插件。它通过记录模型流的首个响应时间、数据块间最长静默和总耗时，结合请求错误与配置的超时值，判断失败更可能来自 DSH 空闲看门狗、SDK、Node HTTP 定时器或模型服务。它还识别上下文超限、空响应、队列、压缩失败和工具超时，并在终端输出判定、证据与建议；可用 /why 查看当前会话及子 agent 的近期结果。可选配置各 provider 的三种超时值和每会话保留数量，默认无需额外服务。

dsh-turn-doctor diagnoses DSH turn failures using request timing to distinguish watchdog, SDK, HTTP, and server timeouts. It also recognizes context, queue, compaction, empty-response, and tool-timeout failures. Verdicts include evidence and fixes; /why lists recent session and subagent results.
DSH 请求超时后，怎么判断是 SDK、HTTP 层还是模型服务的问题？
想根据模型开始响应的时间和流中断间隔定位回合失败原因
DSH 老是报 Request timed out，能不能帮我找出对应的计时器？
让 DSH 在模型请求失败时打印判定依据和建议修复方式
我想查看当前会话最近几次失败诊断，包括子 agent 的结果
能不能分辨模型连接失败、上下文超限和空响应？
How can I tell which timeout layer ended a failed DSH model request?
Show me recent failure diagnoses for this session and its subagents.
dsh-turn-doctor 的功能「按请求时序分类失败」：记录模型流首块到达、最长静默和总时长，并结合错误码及 provider 超时配置判断可能的故障层；失败事件触发诊断并输出证据与建议。
dsh-turn-doctor 的功能「查看近期诊断」：在聊天中调用 /why，汇总当前会话和关联子 agent 最近保留的失败判定、证据与修复建议。
dsh-turn-doctor 的功能「诊断压缩失败」：遇到摘要被 token 上限截断或没有文本摘要时给出对应判定，并提示调整摘要 token 上限或推理设置。
dsh-turn-doctor 的功能「识别工具超时」：收到工具超时结果时关联工具调用名称，报告该工具期限已到并提示检查其 timeoutMs 配置。
dsh-turn-doctor 的功能「分别记录重试诊断」：监听每次重试和回合结束事件，为各次尝试输出诊断；达到重试上限时补充重试耗尽的证据。

dsh-turn-doctor README · dsh-turn-doctor：A diagnostic plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that tells you why a turn failed and which timeout or setting is actually responsible.

dsh-turn-doctor README · Why this exists：A dsh request can time out in several different places:

* dsh's idle watchdog (`streamIdleTimeoutMs`)
* the SDK request timeout (`timeoutMs`)
* Node/undici HTTP timers
* the model server
* individual tool calls

The problem is that the UI usually only shows the final error message, and those messages aren't very specific.

dsh-turn-doctor README · Why this exists：For example, `Request timed out.` might be the SDK timeout or undici's 300-second headers timeout. `terminated` might mean undici gave up waiting for the response body, or the model server died.

That makes it easy to change the wrong setting and then watch the request fail at exactly 5:00 again. This has come up in discussions like #3157 and #4518.

dsh-turn-doctor README · Why this exists：`dsh-turn-doctor` measures each model request itself (time to first byte, longest gap between bytes, and total request time) and uses that timing to identify the most likely failure point.

Example:

dsh-turn-doctor README · Why this exists：```text
turn-doctor: session=session-ccc41e50 turn 1 attempt 1
  verdict: Node's HTTP headers timer (undici) gave up waiting for the server's first response after 300.6 s.
  evidence: no reply bytes in 300.6 s
  fix: install dsh-fetch-timeouts to raise Node's HTTP timers; on llama.cpp this usually means the request was deferred behind a busy slot

It also catches a couple of failures that are otherwise easy to miss, including failed compactions and tool timeouts.

dsh-turn-doctor README · What it detects：| Layer                       | Typical message                                         | Suggested fix                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| dsh idle watchdog           | `pi-ai stream idle timeout after Nms`                   | Raise `streamIdleTimeoutMs`; if the request was queued, check the gate or `--parallel` |
| Node headers timer (undici) | `Request timed out.` with no bytes at ~300 s            | Install/configure `dsh-fetch-timeouts`                                                 |
| SDK request timer           | `Request timed out.` at around `timeoutMs`              | Raise `timeoutMs` on the route                                                         |
| Node body timer (undici)    | `terminated` after ~300 s without data mid-response     | `dsh-fetch-timeouts`, or configure the server to send data/pings                       |
| Server closed/crashed       | `terminated` or `Connection error.` after a short gap

dsh-turn-doctor README · What it detects：Each retry attempt is diagnosed separately. dsh already shows retry countdowns, so turn-doctor doesn't duplicate them.

If the timing isn't enough to distinguish two possible causes, it says that rather than pretending to know.

dsh-turn-doctor README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-turn-doctor
```

That's it.

Verdicts are printed in the dsh terminal. You can also run `/why` in chat to see recent verdicts for the current session, including subagents.

If you've changed your route timeouts from the defaults, add them to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` so turn-doctor can classify failures correctly:

```yaml
- id: turn-doctor
  config:
    providers:
      llamacpp:
dsh-turn-doctor README · Install：If a provider isn't configured, turn-doctor assumes the standard 300-second defaults.

dsh-turn-doctor README · Notes：* turn-doctor only diagnoses failures. It doesn't retry requests, change settings, or inject anything into the model context.
* If the SDK timer and undici headers timer are both set to 300 seconds, a first-byte timeout can be ambiguous. In that case, turn-doctor reports undici because fixing it requires `dsh-fetch-timeouts`; dsh can't change that timer itself.
* Verdicts live in memory for the life of the dsh process (the last few per session, for `/why`). They are not written to the session log: dsh refuses to load a log containing event types it does not know, so a plugin event there would make the session unresumable.
* [dsh-error-lens](https://github.com/Wanbinyu/dsh-error-lens) is related, but solves a different problem: it shows recent failures in a web panel grouped by HTTP status. turn-doctor uses request timing to distinguish the different timeout layers, and also covers compactions and tool calls.
